full_judgment:
9. The suit is on the face of the record is barred by the law of limitation, it is suffered from non-joinder of parties and is also barred by law of estopple, weaver, and acquiescence and the suit is also hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. 

 19. Mr A.M. Aminuddin, learned Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, itself bars filing a suit in a civil court questioning legality of the order passed or any action taken under this Act and thus, the decree passed by the Courts below is a nullity and the High Court Division committed an error of law in maintaining the decree for derequisition. He further submits that in view of section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition Property Act, 1948, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is the owner and possessor of the said quantum of land acquired in LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959 out of which 0.71 acre of land was allotted to the appellant by way of lease agreement in the year 1975 as required for nursery and opening a sale center in the greater interest of the citizens of the Dhaka Metropolitan City. He then submits that there is no scope to say that the suit land is unused and unutilized and the appellant is not the requiring body, and it has been done without jurisdiction. Therefore, the High Court Division committed error of law in affirming the concurrent judgments of the Courts below. He continues to submit that the burden of proof lies upon the plaintiffs to prove the case as alleged and the question of non-service of notices under sections 5(A), 5(C) and 7 of the said Act and non-receiving the compensation money incorporated in the plaint by way of amendment long after 12 years of filing the suit are required to be proved by the plaintiffs which they have utterly failed and, as such, the High Court Division committed an error of law in failing to consider that the amendment was made after a long lapse of time incorporating of those facts with a view to simply making out a case and those facts, as it appears has not been proved. 

 "That section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, itself bars filing a suit in a civil court questioning legality of the order passed or any action taken under this Act and thus, the decree passed by the Courts below is a nullity and the High Court Division committed an error of law in maintaining the decree for derequisition; that the view of section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act,1948 the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh was the owner and possessor of the said quantum of land and out of which 0.71 acre of land was allotted to the petitioner by way of lease agreement in the year 1975 as required for nursery and opening sale center in the greater interest of the citizens of the Dhaka Metropolitan City and in such circumstances it cannot be said that the land is unused and unutilized and the petitioner is not the requiring body, and it has been done without jurisdiction; that the settled principle of law that the burden of proof lies upon the plaintiffs to prove the case as being alleged and the question of non-service of notice under sections 5(A), 5(C) and 7 of the said Act, 1948 and non-receiving the compensation money incorporate in the plaint by way of amendment long after 12 years of filing the suit and the High Court Division committed an error of law in failing to consider that the amendment was made after a long passage of time incorporating of those facts with a view to simply make out a case and those facts, as it appears has not been proved." 

 25. In support of its aforesaid finding, the High Court Division relied upon the case of The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary, Establishement Division, Government of Pakistan Rawalpindi vs Saeed Ahmad Khan, PLD 1974 (SC) 151. In the decision referred to above Hamdur Rahman, CJ held that a malafide act and coram non judice stand on the same footing and no ouster clause in any enactment howsoever widely coached can save them from judicial scrutiny.
